title: Catch a NameError
description:
Source instruction (Exercises: Day 15, item 1): "Open you python interactive shell and try all the examples covered in this section."

NameError example: `print(age)` raises `NameError: name 'age' is not defined` because age was never declared ("we did not define an age variable but we were trying to print it out as if we had had declared it"); it is fixed by first assigning `age = 25`.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `safe_lookup(expr)`, evaluating the given expression string with `eval()` and returning its value, or a string "NameError: <message>" if evaluating it raises a NameError because a name used in the expression is not defined.
examples:
safe_lookup("age") -> "NameError: name 'age' is not defined"
safe_lookup("1 + 1") -> 2
hints: Like SyntaxError, NameError is only raised when the given text is actually evaluated as code, so use eval() on the expression string.
eval() raises NameError when the expression references a variable name that doesn't exist in scope, e.g. eval('age') when age was never assigned.
Wrap eval(expr) in try/except NameError, and in the except branch return an f-string starting with 'NameError: ' followed by the caught exception object.
expected_behavior: Evaluates the given expression string with eval(). If evaluation succeeds, returns the resulting value. If it raises a NameError (an undefined name was referenced), catches it and returns a descriptive string in the form "NameError: <message>" instead of letting the exception propagate.

hidden_tests.label: undefined name 'age', mirrors the source example

explanation: eval() evaluates the given string as a Python expression. Referencing a name that was never assigned, like `age` in the source example, raises NameError; the except block catches it and returns a descriptive string instead of the error propagating.
